edges.description: The only in vivo evidence that THAP11 has a developmental role beyond the metabolic one.
edges.limitations: Depletion rather than the patient's missense allele, so it tests gene requirement and not variant effect, and the patient's F80L protein is known from cell work to retain partial and selective function. The craniofacial phenotype has no reported human counterpart: the single MAHCL patient was not described with cartilage or craniofacial anomalies, which may mean the fish overstates the lesion or simply that nobody looked.

edges.description: Extends the developmental branch from cartilage in fish to ribosome biogenesis in mouse, and reframes the syndrome as part cobalamin disorder and part ribosomopathy.
edges.limitations: No ribosomal or bone marrow phenotype has been sought in the single human MAHCL patient, so the ribosomopathy component is a mouse finding awaiting a human test. It is also derived largely from Hcfc1 rather than Ronin alleles in places, so the split between the two genes' contributions is not resolved.

nodes.description:
Betaine provides an alternative route for remethylating homocysteine to methionine through betaine-homocysteine methyltransferase, bypassing the methylcobalamin-dependent methionine synthase reaction that the cobalamin block disables. GeneReviews names it alongside hydroxocobalamin in the management of thromboembolic complications.
As with everything in this section, no treatment response has been reported for a MAHCL patient. Note also that its rationale is aimed at the homocysteine arm, which the single reported patient's OMIM synopsis says was not raised, so it is the part of the group regimen whose applicability to this disorder is least clear.

evidence.reference_title: Disorders of Intracellular Cobalamin Metabolism.
evidence.snippet: Treatment of thromboembolic complications (e.g., HUS and thrombotic microangiopathy) includes initiation of hydroxocobalamin (OHCbl) and betaine or an increase in their doses.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and biochemical outcome after hydroxocobalamin dose escalation in a series of patients with cobalamin C deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Hydroxocobalamin (OHCbl), betaine, folinic acid, levocarnitine and eventually dietary protein restriction are the main therapeutic approaches.

nodes.description:
A homozygous missense change in the THAP domain, the zinc-finger DNA-binding module shared across the twelve human THAP proteins. The variant was found after MMACHC and HCFC1 had been sequenced and excluded in a patient whose clinical and biochemical picture overlapped cblX, so the gene was reached by elimination plus a mechanistic hypothesis rather than by an unbiased screen.
p.Phe80Leu is the only reported MAHCL allele. No second family, no null allele, and no allelic series exist, so nothing is known about whether other THAP11 variants would give the same disease.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in THAP11 cause an inborn error of cobalamin metabolism and developmental abnormalities.
evidence.snippet: We report a patient who presented with clinical and biochemical phenotypic features that overlap cblX, but who does not have any mutations in either MMACHC or HCFC1.

nodes.description: Because MMACHC sits upstream of the branch point, losing it starves both downstream enzymes at once: methylmalonyl-CoA mutase loses adenosylcobalamin and methionine synthase loses methylcobalamin. That dual failure is what makes the cblC-type disorders "combined", and it is why the biochemical signature is methylmalonic acid plus homocysteine rather than either alone.

evidence.reference_title: An X-linked cobalamin disorder caused by mutations in transcriptional coregulator HCFC1.
evidence.snippet: Defects in cobalamin metabolism lead to disorders characterized by the accumulation of methylmalonic acid and/or homocysteine in blood and urine.

nodes.description:
Dietary protein restriction is part of the group regimen, but the more clinically load-bearing half of this entry is what to avoid, because two of the items are things a clinician unaware of the diagnosis would do routinely.
GeneReviews lists prolonged fasting beyond overnight without dextrose-containing intravenous fluids, protein intake below the age-appropriate allowance or above what a metabolic specialist has prescribed, methionine restriction including medical foods that contain no methionine, and the anaesthetic nitrous oxide. Nitrous oxide is the sharpest of these: it irreversibly oxidises the cobalt of cobalamin and inactivates methionine synthase, so in a patient whose cobalamin processing is already limited it can precipitate acute decompensation. Methionine restriction is the counterintuitive one, since restricting the amino acid a patient is already short of is exactly the wrong move here.
Note the direction of inference. This is management for disorders of intracellular cobalamin metabolism as a class, which MAHCL belongs to by biochemistry; nothing has been reported for a MAHCL patient specifically.

evidence.reference_title: Disorders of Intracellular Cobalamin Metabolism.
evidence.snippet: Agents/circumstances to avoid: Prolonged fasting (longer than overnight without dextrose-containing intravenous fluids); dietary protein intake below the recommended dietary allowance for age or more than that prescribed by a metabolic specialist; methionine restriction including use of medical foods that do not contain methionine; and the anesthetic nitrous oxide.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and biochemical outcome after hydroxocobalamin dose escalation in a series of patients with cobalamin C deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Hydroxocobalamin (OHCbl), betaine, folinic acid, levocarnitine and eventually dietary protein restriction are the main therapeutic approaches.

nodes.description: Mouse models of both members of the complex, made to ask what else the transcriptional lesion deregulates. They reproduce loss of Mmachc, the metabolic perturbation and the developmental defects known from cblC, and additionally show reduced expression of ribosome protein genes with phenotypes attributed to disturbed ribosome biogenesis.

A parallel branch, and the reason MAHCL may not be simply a metabolic disease with a neurological complication. THAP11 loss in zebrafish impairs proliferation and differentiation of neural precursors, and separately abolishes Meckel's cartilage and the pharyngeal cartilages. Mouse work on Hcfc1 and Ronin found the same complex regulating ribosome protein genes, with phenotypes attributed to deregulated ribosome biogenesis rather than to the metabolic block.
How independent this branch really is from the metabolic one is not settled, and the honest answer is less independent than it first looks. In the companion zebrafish work on hcfc1b, the craniofacial abnormalities were rescued by expressing human MMACHC, and the authors concluded that the craniofacial role is mediated in part through MMACHC regulation. So at least some of what looks like a separate developmental program runs back through the same downstream gene as the metabolic lesion. The ribosome biogenesis arm has no such rescue reported and remains the clearest candidate for a genuinely MMACHC-independent contribution.
Whether this branch contributes to the human phenotype is unknown, because there is one patient and no craniofacial or ribosomal assessment was reported for them.

evidence.snippet: Functional analysis in the developing zebrafish embryo demonstrated that both THAP11 and HCFC1 regulate the proliferation and differentiation of neural precursors, suggesting important roles in normal brain development.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in Hcfc1 and Ronin result in an inborn error of cobalamin metabolism and ribosomopathy.
evidence.snippet: In addition to exhibiting loss of Mmachc, metabolic perturbations, and developmental defects previously observed in cblC, we uncovered reduced expression of target genes that encode ribosome protein subunits.

evidence.reference_title: Hcfc1b, a zebrafish ortholog of HCFC1, regulates craniofacial development by modulating mmachc expression.
evidence.snippet: the hcfc1b-mediated craniofacial abnormalities were rescued by expression of human MMACHC, a downstream target of HCFC1 that is aberrantly expressed in cblX

nodes.description:
MMACHC is the cytosolic chaperone that processes incoming cobalamin, removing the upper axial ligand from cyanocobalamin, methylcobalamin and adenosylcobalamin so the cofactor can be routed onward. Without enough of it, dietary and therapeutic cobalamin cannot be converted into the two active forms the cell needs.
This node and everything below it are inherited from cblC biology rather than measured in a MAHCL patient. That is a legitimate inference, because the complementation behaviour and biochemistry of the transcriptional disorders match cblC, but it is an inference and the entry does not present it otherwise.

evidence.reference_title: THAP11F80L cobalamin disorder-associated mutation reveals normal and pathogenic THAP11 functions in gene expression and cell proliferation.
evidence.snippet: Cobalamin disorder is an inborn vitamin deficiency characterized by neurodevelopmental abnormalities, most often owing to biallelic mutations in the MMACHC gene, whose gene product MMACHC is a key enzyme in the cobalamin (vitamin B12) metabolic pathway.

evidence.reference_title: A human vitamin B12 trafficking protein uses glutathione transferase activity for processing alkylcobalamins.
evidence.snippet: MMACHC, a cytosolic cobalamin trafficking chaperone, has been shown recently to catalyze a reductive decyanation reaction when it encounters cyanocobalamin.

evidence.reference_title: A human vitamin B12 trafficking protein uses glutathione transferase activity for processing alkylcobalamins.
evidence.snippet: we demonstrate that this versatile protein catalyzes an entirely different chemical reaction with alkylcobalamins using the thiolate of glutathione for nucleophilic displacement to generate cob(I)alamin and the corresponding glutathione thioether

nodes.description:
Mild methylmalonic aciduria was recorded in the single reported patient. It is milder than in classical cblC, and the OMIM clinical synopsis for this disorder notes it occurred without homocystinuria, which is unusual for a disorder in this group.
The source is the OMIM clinical synopsis recorded in external_assertions, not a quotable sentence: the primary report's cached record is abstract-only and its abstract does not give the patient's biochemistry. This phenotype therefore carries no evidence item rather than one that would attest to something else. The GeneReviews sentence naming methylmalonic acid and total homocysteine as the mainstays of biochemical testing is a testing strategy rather than an observation about this patient, and lives in the diagnosis block.

The only reported MAHCL allele, homozygous in the index patient of Moroccan parentage. It falls in the THAP domain, the zinc-finger DNA-binding module that mediates sequence-specific promoter contact, which is what makes a binding defect the expected consequence rather than a guess.
Recorded as LIKELY_PATHOGENIC rather than PATHOGENIC. The functional support is unusually direct for a single-patient disorder, since promoter binding and MMACHC transcription were measured for this exact allele in HEK-293 cells, but the reporting authors themselves described it as potentially pathogenic and there is no second family and no segregation beyond one homozygote.

The mainstay of treatment across the disorders of intracellular cobalamin metabolism, given parenterally. No treatment response has been reported for a MAHCL patient, so this is the management of the group the disease belongs to rather than an established therapy for it. Whether raising cobalamin availability helps when the lesion is a shortage of the chaperone that processes it is a real mechanistic question, not a formality.

evidence.reference_title: Disorders of Intracellular Cobalamin Metabolism.
evidence.snippet: Critically ill individuals must be stabilized, preferably in consultation with a metabolic specialist, by treating acidosis, reversing catabolism, and initiating parenteral hydroxocobalamin.

nodes.description: MMACHC transcription falls even though the MMACHC gene is intact. This is the same lesion cblX produces through HCFC1, and the two were shown to converge here: HCFC1 and THAP11 act as a complex on the MMACHC promoter, and knocking down either one reduces MMACHC message.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in THAP11 cause an inborn error of cobalamin metabolism and developmental abnormalities.
evidence.snippet: HCFC1 regulates cobalamin metabolism via the regulation of MMACHC expression through its interaction with THAP11, a THAP domain-containing transcription factor.

evidence.reference_title: An X-linked cobalamin disorder caused by mutations in transcriptional coregulator HCFC1.
evidence.snippet: The severe reduction in MMACHC mRNA and protein within subject fibroblast lines suggested a role for HCFC1 in transcriptional regulation of MMACHC, which was further supported by the identification of consensus HCFC1 binding sites in MMACHC.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in Hcfc1 and Ronin result in an inborn error of cobalamin metabolism and ribosomopathy.
evidence.snippet: Since HCFC1/RONIN jointly regulate MMACHC, patients with mutations in these factors suffer from reduced MMACHC expression and exhibit a cblC-like disease.

nodes.description: The step that turns a transcription factor variant into a metabolic disease, and the one place in this entry where the causal claim is directly measured rather than inferred. In HEK-293 cells the F80L protein bound a subset of THAP11 target promoters less well than wild type, and the MMACHC promoter was among the strongly affected ones. Binding was selectively rather than globally impaired, which matters: a transcription factor that had simply stopped working everywhere would not explain a disease whose dominant biochemical signature is a single pathway.

evidence.reference_title: THAP11F80L cobalamin disorder-associated mutation reveals normal and pathogenic THAP11 functions in gene expression and cell proliferation.
evidence.snippet: We show that THAP11F80L selectively affected promoter binding by THAP11, having more deleterious effects on a subset of THAP11 targets, and resulting in altered patterns of gene expression.

nodes.description: Profoundly impaired neurodevelopment with seizures. The phenotype was described as overlapping cblX, and cblX itself is characterised by intractable epilepsy and profound neurocognitive impairment that is more severe than in early-onset cblC. Whether MAHCL tracks cblX or cblC in severity is not established from one patient.

evidence.reference_title: An X-linked cobalamin disorder caused by mutations in transcriptional coregulator HCFC1.
evidence.snippet: A common phenotype of severe neurological symptoms including intractable epilepsy and profound neurocognitive impairment, along with variable biochemical manifestations, was observed in all affected subjects compared to individuals with early-onset cblC.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in THAP11 cause an inborn error of cobalamin metabolism and developmental abnormalities.
evidence.snippet: We sequenced THAP11 by Sanger sequencing and discovered a potentially pathogenic, homozygous variant, c.240C > G (p.Phe80Leu).

evidence.reference_title: Disorders of Intracellular Cobalamin Metabolism.
evidence.snippet: THAP11(cblX-like), ZNF143(cblX-like), or a hemizygous variant in HCFC1 (cblX, which can show a cblC complementation class).

nodes.description: The functional model in the founding report. Loss of THAP11 impairs neural precursor proliferation and differentiation and abolishes Meckel's cartilage, the ceratohyal and all ceratobranchial cartilages, mirroring the craniofacial phenotype the same group had previously shown for HCFC1.
